text:
sam: Heads up — smallbatch p50 shot up ~30% after the CUDA 12.9p2 driver rollout in staging. Not seeing it on large batches.
riley: Ugh. Which workloads? any quick diffs? :eyes:
sam: repro on tinyseq (seq=32, batch=4) perf job: p50 12ms -> 16ms, tails okay. CPU offload tests unaffected.
maria: can you paste the perf traces? I ran the same job and saw an increase in time spent in prefetch_worker and a bunch of host->device enqueue waits.
sam: attaching snippet from perf dump:
```
[profile] kernel: attention_fwd  4.3ms
[profile] kernel: matmul_small 2.1ms
[profile] prefetch_worker:   6.8ms (was 3.2ms before)
[trace] stream 0: enqueue memcpy H2D (queued)
[trace] stream 1: prefetch_worker dispatch -> blocks on scheduling
```

dave: interesting — I saw a similar signal in nightly CI when we bumped the driver earlier. My gut: threadpool affinity/scheduling changed in the driver so our prefetch threads are getting scheduled on compute SMs or contending with kernels.
riley: can you bisect? is it the driver or a Triton/PyTorch change? this was driver-only rollout though.
dave: did a quick two-point: rollback to driver 12.9p1 makes prefetch_worker latency go back down. So driver is the delta.
infra-bot: CI job 81234 failed perf-threshold (regression detected). link: https://ci.internal/jobs/81234
ci-bot: perf test output attached (job 81234). Regression detected on tinyseq workload.
maria: I profiled with nsight and saw prefetch threads migrating between streams. Snapshot: 
```
Thread 140: prefetch_worker -> cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(0, CU_STREAM_NON_BLOCKING)
Thread 140: cudaLaunchKernel(matmul_small, stream 0)  <-- unexpected from prefetch thread
```

riley: That explains enqueue waits. If prefetch thread fires a kernel (accidentally or due to driver scheduling), it can grab CUDA context/SM and stall other streams. Might be driver scheduler misattributing thread-to-stream affinity.
sam: workaround idea — pin prefetch threads to dedicated CPU cores and set `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0`? Not sure that helps.
dave: quick patch idea: change prefetch worker to use `cudaStreamNonBlocking` + explicit host/device memcpy streams and avoid launching any kernels from the prefetch thread. The runtime already sometimes launches small device-side helper kernels from the same thread; we should isolate that.
maria: I tried forcing prefetch worker to `std::thread::native_handle` + sched_setaffinity -> pins to core 4,5; p50 dropped back slightly but still +8%. So partial mitigation.
riley: Sounds like root is driver scheduler change that made kernels launched from host threads block other work. We should: 1) bisect to exact driver build, 2) open driver bug if repro, 3) push quick runtime change to avoid any kernel launches from prefetch threads.
sam: I'll open a minimal repro with a tiny harness that spawns a prefetch thread which issues `cudaMemcpyAsync` + a helper kernel. Will attach.
dave: I'll prepare a small revert/hold on the driver rollout for staging and gate prod until we have an upstream bug or runtime fix.
infra-bot: rollback scheduled for staging at 03:15 UTC if no objections. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: linking bisect artifacts: https://ci.internal/artifacts/driver-bisect/2478129999/
maria: FYI the Nsight timeline shows kernel preemption counts increased and `cuLaunchKernel` from host threads now sometimes takes a scheduling syscall queued wait.
riley: ok next steps: sam to upload repro, dave to prepare temporary rollback policy, maria to draft nsight screenshots + syscall trace, I'll draft a follow-up issue to driver vendor with the minimal repro and timelines.
sam: repro uploaded to the thread (tiny-prefetch-repro.tar.gz). ping me if you can't run it.
dave: agreed. thanks all — let's keep this constrained and prefer the runtime mitigation to avoid customer impact if driver vendor slow to respond. :heart:
